predict.question: In case B, your app's copy of a database starts six writes behind. Each round it receives four new writes and applies six. After four rounds, how many writes are still pending?

exploreHint: Run both cases; compare the changed input.
bookIdea: Designing Data-Intensive Applications distinguishes accepting writes from propagating and applying them across replicas.
modelBoundary: A ends with {A} pending writes; B with {B}. Six applications against four new writes drain the initial six-write backlog, then the zero floor stops depletion. A fixed backlog model; read visibility, ordering, consistency and replication delay in time are not represented.
doesItHoldUp: Does it hold up? Real-world applicability and the connection to the book remain unverified.
